covers.quote: Include all parts of the periodical
Number each issue of a serial and include other publication information so people can find it.
name of the publisher or distributor or both

rules.quote: Because each issue is complete in itself, you must include the following:
rules.specification: Every periodical issue must include front-matter metadata comprising title, year/volume/issue, sponsoring body, publisher/distributor, copyright details, circulation restrictions, and ISSN.
rules.violation_condition: a periodical issue that omits its title; year, volume and issue number; sponsoring body; publisher or distributor; copyright details; circulation restrictions; or ISSN
when: The publication is an issue of a periodical (journal, magazine, or serial).
rules.why: G-1, G-2, G-4: The section heading and list are consolidated into the mandatory rule stated at 37e19355452b.

rules.quote: If the periodical shows page numbers, use odd numbers for the right-hand pages.
rules.violation_condition: an even page number appearing on a right-hand (recto) page in a printed or PDF periodical
when: The periodical is published in print or as a paginated PDF and displays page numbers.
rules.why: Specific typographic/pagination rule for print/PDF periodicals.

rules.quote: In print and PDF periodicals, start each new volume at page 1. Number the pages of the issues so they continue from one issue to the next, throughout the volume.
rules.violation_condition: a new volume of a print or PDF periodical not starting at page 1, or page numbering restarting at 1 within consecutive issues of the same volume rather than continuing sequentially
when: The publication is a print or PDF periodical grouped into volumes.
rules.why: G-1, G-4: Heading is consolidated with the operational instruction in the paragraph.

covers.quote: Repeat all of this information, except for the ISSN, on the first page with the rest of the essential information, such as copyright and any restrictions on circulation.

rules.quote: Include the title, date of issue, International Standard Serial Number (ISSN) and sponsoring body on the outside front cover of the volume.
rules.violation_condition: a bound print volume that omits the title, date of issue, ISSN, or sponsoring body on its outside front cover
when: Issues of a periodical with covers are bound into a print volume.
rules.why: G-2: Covers the front-cover and first-page requirements for bound print volumes.

covers.quote: the volume and part number (if any).

rules.quote: Put the publication details for each issue on the cover page.
rules.violation_condition: a periodical without a separate cover that omits the title, publishing date, sponsoring body, or volume/part number on its cover page
when: The periodical is a print issue without a separate cover (such as a newspaper or magazine).
rules.why: G-1, G-4: The lead-in sentence and list specify required cover-page details for periodicals without separate covers.

rules.quote: Start each issue of a periodical without a separate cover from page 1. Include the title, date and page number at the top or bottom of the page.
rules.violation_condition: an issue of a periodical without a separate cover that does not start from page 1, or that omits the title, date, or page number in the header/footer
when: The periodical is published without a separate cover.
rules.why: G-2: Pagination and running header/footer rule for periodicals without separate covers.

covers.quote: Apply for identifying numbers for your periodical

rules.quote: Use separate ISSNs for a digital periodical and a print periodical, even if they look the same.
rules.violation_condition: using the same ISSN for both the digital and print editions of a periodical
when: A periodical is published in both digital and print formats.
rules.why: G-1, G-4: Concrete rule on assigning distinct ISSNs for print and digital editions.

covers.quote: Explain how to access datasets and extra material

rules.quote: Both printed and digital periodicals must tell their users how to access extra material.
rules.violation_condition: a periodical that refers to supplemental material (such as datasets, code, audio, or video) without providing access information (such as a hyperlink or appendix notice)
when: The periodical incorporates or relies on external supplemental material or datasets.
rules.why: G-1, G-4: Concrete requirement to include access instructions for extra material.
